Inelastic

/in-ih-LAS-tik/ - the stress falls on LAS · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Inelastic means not adjusting or responding when conditions such as price change.

Attendance at the shipyard's licensing exam is inelastic: double the fee and the same three hundred welders sign up, because the license is the only door into the trade.

Worked Example

The stadium doubled the price of bottled water in July and sold the same number of bottles; in August it doubled the price again, and the count barely moved. Thirst in a heat wave, the concessions manager concluded, is almost perfectly inelastic.

Inelastic is more precise than 'steady' or 'unchanging' because it names a relationship, not a state: the quantity people buy refuses to respond when the price moves. If nothing pushed, 'steady' will do; inelastic means something pushed hard and nothing budged.

How Inelastic Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

unresponsive

unresponsive: fails to react to any push, in any setting; inelastic is the economist's version, deaf to price

unbudging

unbudging: refuses to shift no matter what leans on it

Antonyms

sensitive

sensitive: registers even a small nudge and moves with it

springy

springy: stretches and snaps to a new shape the moment conditions push — the picture inelastic denies

How Strong Is It? — sluggish → inelastic → fixed

sluggish vs. inelastic

sluggish vs. inelastic: A sluggish response is slow but real — the quantity drifts eventually, stopping short of inelastic, where the response barely registers at all.

fixed vs. inelastic

fixed vs. inelastic: Fixed goes further than inelastic: not a faint response but none whatsoever, the quantity nailed in place whatever the price does.

Sort It Out

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — in-

Prefix — in-: not

Root — elast-

Root — elast-: able to be driven; springy, stretchable (Greek elastos)

Suffix — -ic

Suffix — -ic: characteristic of

Put it together

Put it together: In- (not) + elast- (Greek elastos, 'able to be driven or set in motion' — springy) + -ic (characteristic of) = not springy: something that will not stretch when pulled. Economists borrowed the rubber-band picture whole. Elastic demand stretches when price pulls at it; inelastic demand is the band gone stiff — pull all you like, it keeps its shape.

Use the root in a new word: elasticity

Use the root in a new word: elasticity: Engineers test the elasticity of the cable by loading it and measuring how far it stretches and springs back.

Root Check

Word Choice

technical / neutral

Inelastic belongs to economics prose — the SAT loves it near charts about prices. Keep it for the price-and-demand relationship; for a person who won't bend, use 'inflexible' or 'unbudging' instead. And note the seam: the in- is a prefix on elastic, making this the one word in the unit where the -ic arrived already attached.
